confirm.archive_remove: Take {what} out of {archive}? The archive is written anew without it; there is no trash inside an archive.
confirm.no_trash_here: No trash on this disk: delete {what} for good?
disk_image.unknown: Its format was not recognized from its header; 7-Zip may still read it.
dupes.before_scan: Pick the folders to compare, then Scan. Nothing goes to the trash without asking.

dupes.confirm_text.one: Move {n} copy ({size}) to the trash? At least one copy of each stays.
dupes.confirm_text.other: Move {n} copies ({size}) to the trash? At least one copy of each stays.

dupes.mark_tip: Mark to move to the trash
error.trash: Could not move {what} to the trash

error.counted_trash.one: {done} of {all} moved to the trash; {n} could not be moved to the trash
error.counted_trash.other: {done} of {all} moved to the trash; {n} could not be moved to the trash

feature.delete.a2: Not every file system has a trash the system can use. The error names the file. Use {delete_forever} to delete it for good, after checking.
feature.delete.q2: Moving to the trash fails on a network share or a USB stick.
feature.delete.what: {delete} moves the marked files to the system's trash; {delete_forever} deletes them for good. Both ask first.
feature.duplicates.a2: They go to the trash, not away for good, and at least one copy of each group always stays. Check with Show first if the folder matters.
feature.duplicates.what: In the desktop app, {duplicates} finds duplicate files and folders by content and moves extra copies to the trash.
feature.move_and_rename.q2: I moved files into a zip. Are the originals in the trash?
feature.undo.a1: A move to the trash, yes, except on a Mac and in the Flatpak, where you restore it from the system's trash. Deleting for good ({delete_forever}) cannot be undone.
feature.undo.a3: No. The history lives in memory, for the app run. After a restart, a move to the trash can still be restored from the system's trash.
feature.undo.what: {undo} undoes the last file operation (copy, move, rename, new folder, trash, pack, extract, permissions and dates), up to 20 back.

stop.done.trash.one: Stopped: {n} of {all} moved to the trash
stop.done.trash.other: Stopped: {n} of {all} moved to the trash

termux.no_trash_storage: No trash on the phone's storage: delete {what} for good?
undo.no_restore: the trash here gives nothing back to apps: restore it from the system's trash
undo.no_restore_hint: {key} cannot bring it back here: restore it from the system's trash
undo.no_trash: cannot go to the trash from here, so it is left as it is
sync.delete: Also delete what is only in {dir} (to the trash)
sync.about: Plan first: every copy, replacement and deletion is listed before anything changes. What is replaced or deleted goes to the trash; {undo} undoes it all.
sync.planned: {n} steps: {copies} to copy, {replaces} to replace, {deletes} to the trash ({size} to copy)
sync.kept: The trash could not take what was replaced or deleted: it is in {path}
feature.compare_folders.a2: From its menu: Make right like left or Make left like right plans every copy, replacement and deletion first, sends what it replaces or deletes to the trash, and {undo} undoes it. Or mark the differences and press {copy}. On Windows, and on a disk the bin could only copy to, it stays in a .coxswain-sync-… folder at the target's top instead.
sync.moved_away: The folder holding what was replaced or deleted was moved during the run, so it is not in the trash: {path}
